name: Lateral Shuffle to Medicine Ball Throw
definition: A unilateral power repetition that begins side-on to a medicine-ball-safe rebound wall or prepared partner, uses a short non-crossing lateral shuffle toward the target, plants in an athletic stance, and immediately releases a two-hand rotational medicine-ball throw. The repetition ends at release; catching the return is not part of the rep. Stationary throws, crossover approaches, continuous shuffles, floor slams, and chest passes remain outside this family.

variantAxes.description: The reviewed locomotor entry without a fixed step count.
The relationship between travel and target.
The planted stance used for release.
Whether an external guide constrains the ball.

exercises.name: Lateral Shuffle to Medicine Ball Throw
aliases: Shuffle to Rotational Medicine Ball Throw

execution.startingPosition: Stand side-on to a medicine-ball-safe rebound wall or prepared partner in a shallow athletic stance with the ball in both hands near the hip away from the target.
execution.movement: Take a short, quick sideways shuffle toward the target without crossing the feet, load the ball near the outside hip, plant both feet, rotate, and release immediately.
execution.endpoint: The repetition ends when the ball leaves both hands toward the target around mid-torso height.
execution.returnPhase: Retrieve the ball or receive it after the repetition, walk back to the marked start, and rebuild the same stance before the next approach.
execution.controlledJoints: Keep the knees aligned with the feet through the shuffle and establish the two-foot plant before releasing.
execution.supportAndPosture: Stay low enough to change direction under control and keep the travel lane clear.
disqualifyingCompensations: Crossing one foot behind the other changes the approach into the crossover variation.
Continuing to shuffle through the release removes the planted throw base.
Catching and immediately returning the ball changes the repetition topology.
execution.sideOrDirection: Complete approaches from one side, then mirror the start and perform equal repetitions from the other direction.
